scenario_prompt: Write the response to this scored RFP question, worth 25% of the RFP's overall technical score: "Describe the migration approach and cutover plan." Context: the migration moves load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances, 620 Hyper-V virtual machines) onto Google Cloud (Google Compute Engine for compute, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer), within a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme, with proposals due 2026-11-15 and the buyer's next compliance audit opening in 6 months. Return only the answer text, no section headers beyond what the answer itself needs.
text:
**RFP and RFI response**

No customer source material (RFP question text, discovery notes) was supplied for this task, so the provenance override in PF-3.3 cannot fire; every term below is judged by the deletion test alone.

Today, load-matching and carrier-settlement run on 28 on-premises Microsoft SQL Server instances across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines. After migration, both systems run on Google Compute Engine with Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL as the data layer, inside a stated 2-year, $4,200,000 programme.

The migration moves in phases mapped to VM and database groupings, not as a single cutover event. Each phase carries its own rollback point, so a failed validation on one instance group does not block or reverse work already completed on another. [PF-2.4 GAP: the phase count, sequencing logic, and per-phase VM/instance groupings were not supplied and are not stated here.]

The buyer's next compliance audit opens in 6 months from today. The migration plan sequences work so that the systems under audit scope remain on their current, already-audited platform until after that audit closes, and moves to Google Cloud only once the audit window has passed. [PF-2.4 GAP: which systems fall inside the audit's scope, and whether load-matching or carrier-settlement is among them, was not supplied.]

Cutover for each phase follows dual-run validation: the target Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance runs in parallel with the source SQL Server instance, and output is compared before traffic switches. [PF-1.17: this comparable requires a named validation method and tooling the vendor can actually produce — none was supplied.] [PF-2.4 GAP: the comparison method, tooling, and acceptance threshold for declaring a match were not supplied.]

Rollback for each phase reverts traffic to the source SQL Server instance and Hyper-V VM group, which stays live and unmodified until its phase's cutover is confirmed. [PF-2.4 GAP: the maximum time window in which rollback must be executable was not supplied.]

| Validation method/tooling for dual-run comparison not named | PF-1.17 / PF-2.4 | A named, checkable comparison method and tool the vendor will use for cutover validation |
| Rollback time window not stated | PF-2.4 | The maximum allowable rollback window per phase |
